For each sequence the following metric is computed:

difficulty(seq) = mean(MSE_prediction)

All sequences are then sorted by difficulty. Extreme values are removed using quantile clipping, and the validation subset is selected from sequences that uniformly cover the remaining difficulty range.

part.text:
1. Causal running-MSE adaptive pair weight — serve existing 2×h256 q8vnni members (42 us/row each, 94.5 us/row pair loaded) plus per-row gate. Mechanism: winner's trick; member that erred recently gets down-weighted, exploits non-overlapping errors (member pairwise corr 0.95–0.99). Change: data none; inference adds causal exp-average of squared residual proxy (running |pred_A−pred_B| and running volatility as MSE proxy, no labels needed) → softmax weight w=σ(β·(eB−eA)), β fit on fold-1 banked predictions only, half-life ~200 rows. Expected: +0.0015±0.002 vs static 0.5/0.5 (static pair saturated +0.002 in biased greedy test); near-zero GPU. Cost: 0 GPU-h, ~2 CPU-h grid over β/half-life. Falsifier: adaptive ≤ static mean on fold-1 banked + fold-0 transfer.

2. Regime lookup-table FiLM gate on fixed pair — tiny meta-learner, no third member. Mechanism: Denisalpino FiLM + class-predictability finding (class 99.4% readable in 500 rows); optimal member varies by class/age/volatility. Change: offline, bin causal regime (class 0–3 × age quartile × fast-clock rate quartile = 64 cells) on banked out-of-fold preds, store per-cell per-target weights (128 floats); serving does table lookup + linear blend (~0.5 us/row). Expected: +0.0010±0.002; captures class-3 vs rest differences static blend misses. Cost: 0 GPU-h. Falsifier: lookup ≤ static blend on fold-0 cells fit on fold-1.

3. LightGBM tabular teacher distilled into GRU student — big offline model, zero serving cost. Mechanism: trees capture threshold/cross-sectional interactions (asymmetry, kurtosis, w3/w21 rank/corr per sibling w3/w13/w21 recipe) that smooth GRU misses; diversity transfers via soft targets. Change: build ~120 causal windowed features (rolling vol/EMA/lag-diff/rank/trend w3/w13/w21 + cross-sectional asymmetry/kurtosis/corr w3/w21, corr≥0.9 prune), train LightGBM per target on scored rows (train + out-of-fold valid), add predictions as 5th distill family coef 0.1–0.15, student `--distill-alpha 0.7 --init c20261003_combo_s3_f1@ep3 --epochs 3`. Expected: +0.0015±0.0025 (uncorrelated-error family worth more than 5th GRU). Cost: ~4 CPU-h GBM + 0.75 GPU-h student. Falsifier: GBM-family student ≤ 4-family student mean (2 seeds) and GBM alone < 0.60 fold-1.

4. Stage-2 residual GBM teacher (sibling 2-stage boosting, offline). Mechanism: stage-1 GRU error is partly predictable from regime; stage-2 fits residual, distills correction without serving 2 models. Change: fit GBM on residuals (true − stage-1 OOF pred) with same windowed + regime features (age, class, clock-rate, running vol); teacher target = stage-1 blend + λ·GBM_resid (λ 0.2–0.4 tuned on fold-1), distill into same student recipe as #3. Expected: +0.0010±0.0025; smaller than #3 because residuals are noisier. Cost: ~4 CPU-h + 0.75 GPU-h. Falsifier: residual-augmented student ≤ plain-blend student; GBM residual R² ≤ 0 on held-out components.

5. Single-served stack distillation with per-target weights — ensemble gain at 1-member CPU. Mechanism: t0/t1 behave differently (t1 consistently +0.01 over t0); single static weight is suboptimal; distilling the gated/static ensemble's outputs (not the mean) into one h256 recovers most of #1–#2 gain at 42 us/row. Change: teacher cache = per-target-optimised blend of 4 families + adaptive-pair outputs from #1 (weights fit per target on fold-1 OOF), student same 3-epoch warm-start recipe, `--distill-family-target-mode raw`. Expected: +0.0010±0.002 over current 0.6692, i.e. ~60% of 2-member gain in 1 member. Cost: 0.75 GPU-h. Falsifier: stack-distilled single ≤ mean-blend single on matched seeds.

6. Block-masked autoencoder pretraining on train+valid streams, then supervised finetune. Mechanism: sibling MAE on full 517 seqs worked; learns clock-block dynamics without labels; valid rows used only as inputs (reconstruction), labels never touched, so fold-1 evaluation stays valid-ish. Change: pretrain 2×256 GRU encoder + light decoder, mask whole clock blocks (cols 0–21/44–47/52–69) at 20% rows, reconstruct masked inputs, 4–6 epochs on train+all-valid inputs; finetune supervised 3-epoch OneCycle/Muon recipe from pretrained encoder. Expected: +0.0015±0.003 (high variance; sibling LB +0.004 but ours is local fold-1). Cost: ~2.5 GPU-h. Falsifier: pretrained init ≤ scratch mean over 2 seeds, or linear probe reconstruction R² < 0.3 on held-out components.

7. Next-step GRU feature-extractor pretraining (AlexKlos trick), frozen as side input. Mechanism: next-row prediction forces learning tradable dynamics; frozen hidden state becomes a causal regime embedding the main GRU consumes. Change: train small GRU-128 to predict next-row 112 cols (MSE) on full streams 3 epochs; freeze it, feed its hidden (projected to 32-d) concatenated to main 211 inputs (243 total), train main teacher 3 epochs from scratch; extractor never sees labels.
